page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is categorized as weak at 3990.37, and large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes are also weak, measuring 36.35 GB/sec and 25.49 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations perform weakly at 5.68 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is average at 7.76 GB/sec.

The L4s_v4 offers a high local storage-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring fast local NVMe storage without massive multi-core scaling. Tradeoffs include lower multi-threaded efficiency and constrained memory bandwidth. This hardware profile is suited for database operations, text processing, and single-threaded tasks, but is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications or medium-to-large language model inference.
